tools.name: fetch_html
tools.description:
Exposes POST /html. Returns the page's HTML after JavaScript has run and
redirects have been followed — the DOM a real browser sees, not the empty
shell curl returns. 1 credit.

tools.name: capture_screenshot
tools.description:
Exposes POST /screenshot. Captures the whole rendered page as a PNG —
JavaScript executed, web fonts and images included, exactly as a browser
would draw it. 1 credit, whichever options you use.

Use it to see a page rather than read it: layout, visual regressions,

tools.name: capture_pdf
tools.description:
Exposes POST /pdf. Prints the whole rendered page to a PDF — JavaScript
executed, web fonts and lazy-loaded images included, its headings as
bookmarks. 1 credit, whichever options you use.

Use it to archive or hand on a page as a document: a receipt, an article,
a report, terms as they stood today.

tools.name: capture_console_errors
tools.description:
Exposes POST /console. Loads the page in headless Chrome and returns
what it reported through console.error and console.warn during load, plus
uncaught exceptions and unhandled promise rejections (not console.log). 1 credit.

What you would open DevTools for: broken third-party scripts and
client-si

tools.name: run_lighthouse_audit
tools.description:
Exposes POST /lighthouse. Runs a real Google Lighthouse audit against the
live page: performance, accessibility, best-practices and SEO scores plus
Core Web Vitals. 2 credits — dearer than a page fetch because the audit
runs in its own limited lane, so it also takes longer than anything else
here.

not by raw frequency. 15 credits.

tools.description:
Exposes POST /summarize. Returns a concise Markdown summary of the page's
main content, with the navigation, ads and boilerplate left out.

The most expensive operation we sell, at 17 credits, because it runs a
language model over the page. If YOU are the model that will read it,

tools.name: extract_data
tools.description:
Exposes POST /extract. Reads the page and fills an object YOU define:
pass `fields`, each with a name, a type and a description of what to take
from the page, and get back exactly those keys in that order. Anything the
page does not give comes back null — values are never guessed.
Types: string, num

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: fetch_markdown, fetch_html, capture_screenshot, capture_console_errors, run_lighthouse_audit, extract_metadata, detect_technologies, summarize_page, extract_data, scrape_url · Private data: list_projects, capture_pdf, detect_technologies, extract_data, get_result, list_requests · Public sink: fetch_markdown, fetch_html, capture_screenshot, capture_pdf, capture_console_errors, run_lighthouse_audit, extract_metadata, detect_technologies, extract_keywords, summarize_page, extract_data, scrape_url, get_request · Destructive: get_usage, fetch_html, run_lighthouse_audit.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: fetch_markdown, fetch_html, capture_screenshot, capture_console_errors, run_lighthouse_audit, extract_metadata, detect_technologies, summarize_page, extract_data, scrape_url · Private data: list_projects, capture_pdf, detect_technologies, extract_data, get_result, list_requests · Public sink: fetch_markdown, fetch_html, capture_screenshot, capture_pdf, capture_console_errors, run_lighthouse_audit, extract_metadata, detect_technologies, extract_keywords, summarize_page, extract_data, scrape_url, get_request · Destructive: get_usage, fetch_html, run_lighthouse_audit

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "extract_metadata" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
